title: Release all 60 molded tablets from a Torpac tablet-mold plate onto parchment without crumbling any
instruction: Release all sixty tablets from the mold plate onto the parchment without breaking any, and set down anything you pick up.
context: Laboratory formulation and R&D: molding small batches of tablets by hand is a routine bench step in tablet formulation development, compounding and supplement labs; Torpac sells this 60-tablet mold "For Use in R&D, Pharmacy Compounding, Nutritional Supplements". Its release step: "Invert & rest Mold Plate at an angle and use Spreader to push out tablets." The tablets "are more fragile than standard tablets": too light a push leaves them stuck; pressing hard or knocking the plate crushes them.
setup: Millimetres from the midpoint between the two arm bases (x forward, y to the robot's left); heights above the counter. Torpac ProMold RDTM2G X-MRDT60x075 cavity plate, black hard-anodized PTFE-coated aluminium, 120 x 152 x 3.7 (166 g, estimate), upside down at centre (300, 0), long side along y: 60 tapered through-holes, 6 across x 10 along at 12.5 x 14 pitch (estimate), 5.5 mm narrow ends up, 6.5 mm wide ends down, each holding one 75 mg blank rapid-dissolve tablet, its back face just below the plate's back face (16.6 up). The plate rests on two 1/2 in (12.7) square 6061 aluminium bars, 152.4 long (66 g each), standing along y on a 260 x 300 baking-parchment sheet centred at (300, 0), bar centres at x 246.35 and 353.65. The mold's white Powder Spreader (rigid plastic card 90 x 70 x 3 with a rounded lower edge, 18 g; size estimated) stands upright, its 90 mm length along x, in the 4.5 mm slot of a 100 x 40 x 20 wooden block (slot floor 5 up) at (220, -200). Lot B: the block and spreader at (410, -190); everything else as lot A. Trials alternate A, B and are averaged; the screenshot shows lot A.
scoring: Read from the overhead, side and end-on (under the plate) videos, a 5 kg load cell or peak-hold scale under the parchment (tared with everything in place), a photo of the parchment after the plate is lifted off, and a 0.5 mm scale with a 10x loupe. Score 0 for the whole trial if, at any moment: the scale reads over 612 g above the tare (6 N pushed down on the plate by the spreader and grippers together); a gripper touches a tablet; any tablet is cracked, chipped (a missing piece 0.5 mm or more) or crushed; the plate slides over 10 mm or tilts over 5 degrees; or a tablet falls off the counter. The simulation applies the same rules: push and touch from contact forces at every physics step, plate and counter from poses at every control step. Otherwise count the tablets out of their holes and lying still on the parchment with their top at most 5 mm up; every score needs both hands at least 30 mm from the plate, the bars, the parchment under the plate and the spreader for the last 1 s. 0-14 tablets: 0. 15-29: 0.25. 30-44: 0.5. 45-59, or all 60 with something still moving: 0.75. 1.0: all 60, with the plate, spreader and tablets moving under 1 mm for 1 s. A tablet in its hole, on its edge, off the parchment or held does not count. Trials on lots A and B are averaged.
run_limit: 1,600 steps (80 s at 20 Hz) per trial; two trials (lots A and B), averaged
reset_notes: Mold the batches before the session, one per trial, so a reset takes about 2 minutes. 1. Mold 60 blank tablets per plate with a no-active-ingredient rapid-dissolve base by the maker's steps 1-8 (fill, tamp, bake 30 min at 110 C, cool 5-10 min, loosen the thumb screws, lift the cavity plate), or air-dried triturates in printed plates (README). 2. Stand the load-cell platform on the counter at (300, 0), lay the parchment on it and stand the two bars on the parchment along y at x 246.35 and 353.65; heights are then taken from the platform top. 3. Set a molded plate upside down on the bars centred at (300, 0), long side along y; photograph its back face (all 60 tablets in place and whole); tare. 4. Stand the spreader in the block's slot, its length along x, block at the lot's position (A: 220, -200; B: 410, -190). 5. After the trial lift the plate off, photograph the parchment over a numbered 6 x 10 grid with a 0.5 mm scale, and check each tablet with the loupe.
fidelity: True size from the maker's brochure (plate 120 x 152, holes 5.5/6.5 mm by 3.7 mm, 75 mg tablets); pitch, masses, frictions and spreader size are estimates. Holes and tablets are 8-sided; tablets sit 0.1 mm below the back face. Declared rule, not measured: a tablet stays in its hole until the spreader's edge passes over it pressing at least 1 N on the plate, then drops; over 6 N, or any gripper contact on a tablet, counts as crushing. Fixed layouts allow a replay.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (lots A and B 0 each; both ran to the 1,600-step limit without refusing; the arms never came near the spreader or plate); demo: 1.0 in each of lots A and B (all 60 tablets freed onto the parchment, none crushed, spreader laid down, hands clear; full score at 27.2 s)
